patches.old: Ligand binding activates **gustducin** (a Gi-like G protein), ultimately increasing intracellular Ca²⁺ and triggering neurotransmitter release.
patches.new: Ligand binding activates **gustducin** (a Gi-like G protein), whose βγ subunits activate **phospholipase C-β2**. PLCβ2 generates **IP₃**, which releases Ca²⁺ from intracellular stores; the rise in Ca²⁺ opens the **TRPM5** channel, depolarising the cell and triggering transmitter release. The same PLCβ2 cascade is shared by bitter and umami, which is why a single mutation downstream of the receptors can knock out all three of these tastes at once while leaving salty and sour intact.

patches.old: Anosmia can also result from COVID-19 infection, which damages olfactory epithelium.
patches.new:
Anosmia can also result from COVID-19 infection, which damages olfactory epithelium.

One further point that MCAT questions exploit: not everything you smell is olfaction. Free nerve endings of the **trigeminal nerve (CN V)** in the nasal mucosa detect chemical irritants — ammonia, the sting of chlorine, the cool of menthol, the burn of capsaicin. This **chemesthetic** pathway bypasses the olfactory epithelium and bulb entirely, so a patient with a destroyed olfactory bulb still reacts to ammonia while being unable to identify any ordinary odour. That dissociation is how clinicians distinguish true anosmia from malingering.

visual.title: Taste, smell, the two tracts and the gate
visual.alt: Taste divided by transduction mechanism into the G protein tastes, salt through ENaC and sour through OTOP1, with their cranial nerves; smell shown reaching piriform cortex, amygdala and entorhinal cortex without a thalamic relay; a schematic cord contrasting the dorsal column pathway, which ascends on the same side and crosses in the medulla, with the spinothalamic tract, which crosses at entry; and the dorsal horn gate, opened by small pain fibres and closed by large touch fibres.
visual.caption: One pathway crosses at the top, the other at the bottom. That single difference is what makes a cord hemisection produce losses on opposite sides of the body.
